audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed final stress; word = optional light presyllable + heavier-stressed main syllable, max two syllables) rests on the primary SIL phonemic description Cooper & Cooper 1966, which we hold as a full scan with scanned; the deciding passage is confirmed verbatim on p. 93 §2. Glottolog lists only four descriptive refs (all Cooper 1965-1971, all held) plus the 2023 Payap MA thesis; no reference grammar, JIPA illustration or instrumental study of Halang surfaced in Glottolog, the SIL archive listing, Crossref, or the Payap thesis list. The sesquisyllabic North Bahnaric word shape makes the final-stress coding structurally robust, and nothing seen suggests the 2023 thesis would change it; it is worth obtaining only to upgrade recency and check cross-variety consistency. sources.quote: p. 93: "A word may consist of one or two syllables. There are two types of syllables : the 'main syllable' and the 'preliminary syllable'. The 'main syllable' receives the heavier stress and has a maximum pattern of GCLVC. (G stands for glottals, ? and h; and L stands for liquids w, l, r, y.) The 'preliminary syllable' receives the lighter stress and has a pattern of CV or CVC (sometimes GCLVC when there is reduplication) in which the vowel is usually a mid-central vocoid.
